items.text: Two-factor authentication is required for every organization member, outside collaborator, and billing manager.
Organization owners sign in with phishing-resistant authenticators (passkeys or security keys), not TOTP or SMS alone.
SAML single sign-on is configured for the organization and linked to members' identities. Applies where the organization's plan provides SAML.
An IP allow list limits access to the organization to known networks. Requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
Email notifications to organization members are restricted to verified or approved domains.
Base permissions for organization members are set to None.
Members cannot create public repositories; creating private repositories is limited to organization owners.
Only owners can invite outside collaborators, and outside collaborators' repository access is reviewed at least quarterly.
The organization has at least two owners and no more than three.
Publication of GitHub Pages sites from organization repositories is prohibited, or limited to privately published sites.
OAuth app access restrictions are enabled, so third-party OAuth applications reach organization resources only after owner approval.
Only owners can approve GitHub App installations and OAuth app access requests for the organization.
Fine-grained personal access tokens require owner approval before they can access organization resources.
Personal access tokens that can reach the organization are inventoried and reviewed; stale, unused, or ownerless tokens are revoked.
Deploy keys are disabled for the organization's repositories; any exception is inventoried with an owner and a review date.
Every installed GitHub App is inventoried with a named internal owner; apps nobody owns are uninstalled.
GitHub Actions is limited to actions and reusable workflows created by GitHub and verified creators, or to an owner-approved allowlist.
The default permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN are read-only for the organization.
Workflow runs from forks require approval for every outside contributor, not only first-time contributors.
The retention period for Actions artifacts and logs is set to 90 days or less.
Self-hosted runners are never used by public repositories, and runner groups limit self-hosted runners to named repositories.
Organization Actions secrets are scoped to selected repositories; no secret is shared with all repositories unless its exposure is recorded as accepted.
Secret scanning is enabled by default for new repositories in the organization.
Push protection for secret scanning is enabled by default for new repositories in the organization.
Dependabot alerts and Dependabot security updates are enabled by default for new repositories in the organization.
An organization ruleset requires a pull request with at least one approval and required status checks before merging to a default branch.
Private vulnerability reporting is enabled for the organization's repositories.
Private repositories cannot be forked to accounts outside the organization.
Organization webhooks are inventoried; each active webhook has a stated purpose and a named owner.
Every organization webhook has a secret set and SSL verification enabled.
Webhooks deliver only to endpoints the organization operates; inactive and failing webhooks are removed.
The organization audit log is reviewed at least monthly for security events: owner and member changes, token and app grants, and settings changes.
The audit log attributes events to actors and tokens: IP addresses are displayed and token-performed events are identifiable.
Security-relevant audit events are exported or otherwise retained beyond the audit log's own retention window.
